svg.title: Five envelopes, five questions
svg.desc: A whiteboard sketch showing a packet as five nested rectangles labelled Ethernet, IP, TCP, TLS and HTTP wrapped around a scrap of JSON, with the single question each layer answers written beside it and the header sizes of 14, 20 and 20 bytes noted, next to a measured timeline of one real HTTPS request broken into 4 millisecond DNS, 22.6 millisecond TCP, 32.5 millisecond TLS and 29.6 millisecond request segments totalling 88.7 milliseconds, the same timeline again with the first three segments crossed out under keep-alive, and a seven-hop traceroute reaching a CDN edge in 20.3 milliseconds.
svg.text: 54 bytes of header before ONE byte of payload
packet fragments - or is dropped and
you get to debug that at 2am.
each layer answers exactly ONE question
"which process - and did it all arrive?"
and none of them knows the others exist.
TTFB = 88.7 ms. Only 29.6 ms of it was the actual request.
the SECOND request on the same connection:
keep-alive: DNS, TCP and TLS all disappear. 29.6 ms, not 88.7.
the "server" is 20.3 ms away, not 200 - anycast put a copy near you
the layers do not cost the same. Look at which segment
is actually big before you optimise anything.
...and if a packet is lost? -> Module 2
